perf.summary: (1 << k) is recomputed in the loop condition and in every index expression; row base i*(1<<k) and the f[row+mask] target are recomputed repeatedly inside the submask loop.
perf.currentCost: Per innermost iteration: two shifts for the two (1<<k) factors in f[i*(1<<k)+sub] and g[sub*(1<<k)+mask], plus i*(1<<k) and the f[...+mask] load/compare each repeated though mask is fixed across the sub-loop. The for-mask condition reevaluates (1<<k) every iteration.
perf.proposedChange: Hoist int size = 1 << k; once. Precompute long* fRow = f + i*size; long* gBase = g; before the mask loop. Inside the mask loop hoist long* fTarget = fRow + mask; long best = *fTarget; then in the sub loop compute long val = fRow[sub] + g[sub*size + mask]; if (val < best) best = val; and write *fTarget = best; once after the sub loop. Compare against 2^k literal-free bound.
perf.rationale: Replaces repeated shifts/multiplies with hoisted invariants, turns the read-modify-write of f[row+mask] (which has a memory dependency chain) into a single register accumulator written once, and removes the (1<<k) recompute in the loop bound. Fewer ops and a shorter dependency chain in the hottest loop of an O(3^k) algorithm.
perf.risk: Caching best in a register and writing once is safe because f[i*size+mask] is not read elsewhere within this mask iteration (sub<mask guarantees the read indices fRow[sub] and the column g[...+mask] are distinct cells from the written cell). Behavior identical.

perf.summary: The branch `if (sub < mask)` inside the submask enumeration is always true for proper submasks generated by `sub = (mask-1)&mask` then `(sub-1)&mask`, except it guards equality which never occurs in this enumeration.
perf.currentCost: One compare+branch per innermost iteration across O(3^k) iterations.
perf.proposedChange: The standard submask enumeration `for (sub = mask; sub > 0; sub = (sub-1)&mask)` starting from `(mask-1)&mask` never yields sub==mask, so sub<mask is implied by sub>0 here (the loop already starts strictly below mask). Drop the `if (sub < mask)` guard, or if the intent is to exclude only sub==mask, note it is already excluded. Verify k small enough that sub stays positive.
perf.rationale: Removes a predictably-taken branch from the innermost loop, shortening the per-iteration critical path and helping Burst keep the loop tight/vectorizable-friendly.
perf.risk: Must confirm the enumeration never produces sub>=mask. Since sub is seeded with (mask-1)&mask (strictly a proper submask) and each step masks with mask while decrementing, sub is always a proper submask < mask. If any reachable mask makes the guard meaningful, keep it. Default to keeping unless verified.
